title: Inducing Process Supervision from Outcome-Only Reinforcement Learning
data_curation: Training uses only trajectory-level outcome labels, no step annotations. Math domain: 3,200 trajectories sampled from the public SCAN-Pro dataset (built from the MATH training set). Agent domain: an RL corpus of 2,905 multi-turn trajectories from HotpotQA, GAIA, tau2-Bench and BFCL, decontaminated against AgentProcessBench by dropping trajectories whose task-prompt 5-gram Jaccard similarity exceeds 0.8. Reward is rule-based and binary: 1 if the parsed outcome label matches the ground-truth trajectory correctness D, else 0; the generated step labels are never scored. Matched-data baselines (AutoPSV, ImplicitPRM) are re-implemented at both 3.2K and 197K trajectories for comparison.
curriculum: Not a focus of this paper. TIPS is a single-stage outcome-only RL run on an off-the-shelf instruct or thinking backbone (no SFT or distillation warm-start), trained for 1 epoch. The authors propose a label-free early-stopping heuristic instead of a schedule: stop when ORM accuracy plateaus and response length starts to decline, because weaker priors (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct) see ProcessBench F1 peak early (+25.7 at step 30) and decay (+9.4 at step 90) while ORM accuracy keeps rising.
method: TIPS (Thinking-Induced Process Supervision) trains a generative reward model with outcome-only RL. Given a problem and a candidate solution split into indexed paragraphs, the model writes a CoT, then a JSON with per-step labels (1 valid / 0 invalid or dependent on an earlier error) and a final outcome label. Reward uses only the outcome label; under GRPO the same group-relative advantage is applied to every token (CoT, step labels, outcome label), so thoughts that track step validity, and therefore predict the outcome correctly, get reinforced. At test time the step labels serve directly as PRM output. GRPO variant: advantage not divided by group std, token-mean clipped surrogate, KL coefficient 0, AdamW, LR 1e-6, batch 32, max response 16K tokens, verl on 8 A800s. An information-theoretic bound (via Fano) gives I(Z;Y|R) >= H(D|R) - H_b(P_e) - H(D|Y,R), predicting weak transfer when there are input shortcuts, high outcome error, or loose step-outcome coupling.
eval_metrics: ProcessBench F1 (GSM8K, MATH, OlympiadBench, OmniMath subsets); AgentProcessBench First-Error Accuracy (HotPotQA, GAIA, BFCL, tau2-Bench); Best-of-8 reranking accuracy over Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct samples on GSM8K, MATH, College Math, OlympiadBench, Minerva (vs Majority Vote@8 and Pass@8 oracle); mean@4 solver accuracy on AIME 2026 and HMMT Feb 2026 as a control. Headline: TIPS-Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 reaches 85.2 ProcessBench F1 (base 60.3) and TIPS-Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 77.7 (base 63.8). Best-of-8 average 73.3 vs 78.1 oracle. AgentProcessBench average gains are +2.5 / +5.4 / +4.5 for Qwen3-4B-Instruct / 4B-Thinking / 8B-Thinking. A 60-trajectory human study found correct first-error localization in 78.3% of cases.
key_results: Using only 3.2K outcome-labeled trajectories, TIPS-Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 scores 85.2 ProcessBench F1, beating Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-72B (78.3), GenPRM-32B (77.6), GPT-5.4-Instruct (79.4) and Claude-4.7-Opus (79.3), though not o1-mini (87.9). Outcome-supervised ImplicitPRM and AutoPSV trained on 197K trajectories reach only 41.5 and 45.3 F1. A label-only prompt (no CoT) gains just +0.7 F1 versus +13.9 with CoT, and solver-format RLVR on DAPO-Math-17K does not improve ProcessBench at all (62.8).
evolution_note: TIPS sits between the PRM line (PRM800K human labels, Math-Shepherd/SCAN Monte Carlo labels, GenPRM/ThinkPRM distilled generative PRMs) and the reasoning-reward-model line (RM-R1, J1) that applies RLVR to ORMs. It reacts to the cost and label drift of MC estimation, and to the poor step localization of outcome-supervised implicit PRMs (ImplicitPRM, AutoPSV), by showing that GRPO on an outcome-only verdict yields a strong PRM as a byproduct when step and outcome correctness are tightly coupled. It points toward cheap generative verifiers for math and, with weaker transfer so far, for agent trajectories.
